content.value_statement: Modern Angular projects require many new patterns across Signals, routing, SSR, and hydration. This skill gives practical guidance for building and migrating Angular applications with current architecture.
actual_capabilities: Guides Signals, computed values, effects, signal inputs, and signal outputs.
Explains standalone components, lazy routing, functional guards, and route resolvers.
Covers zoneless setup, OnPush change detection, and performance patterns.
Provides SSR, hydration, defer blocks, and TransferState guidance.
Compares modern Angular patterns with legacy NgModule and decorator patterns.
Shows forms, testing, and state management patterns through TypeScript examples.
limitations: It does not execute Angular CLI commands or verify builds by itself.
It focuses on Angular v20+ and is not intended for AngularJS migration.
Examples use placeholder APIs and need project-specific review.
It does not replace official Angular release notes for breaking changes.

use_cases.title: Modernize an Angular App
use_cases.description: Refactor NgModule-era components toward standalone components, Signals, and current dependency injection patterns.

use_cases.title: Plan SSR and Hydration
use_cases.description: Design rendering, hydration, and defer strategies for a faster Angular application.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Coding Sessions
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code Angular-specific patterns for components, routing, forms, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Modern Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new Angular component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a standalone Angular component using Signals, signal inputs, and OnPush change detection. Explain the key design choices.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Local State
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Angular component from manual local state to Signals. Keep behavior unchanged and list any migration risks.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Rendering Performance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for SSR and hydration planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Angular route for SSR, hydration, and defer opportunities. Recommend changes that improve startup performance.

prompt_templates.title: Design Zoneless Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased plan to migrate this Angular application toward zoneless change detection. Include testing and rollback checkpoints.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to modernize a component that uses decorator inputs and manual subscriptions.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a migration plan using signal inputs, computed state, cleanup guidance, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A team wants faster initial loads for an Angular product page.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends SSR, hydration checks, defer boundaries, and TransferState use for API data.

output_examples.input: An AI coding session needs Angular-specific routing guidance.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines standalone routes, lazy loading, functional guards, resolvers, and testing considerations.

best_practices: Share the Angular version and current project structure before asking for changes.
Ask for migration steps that preserve behavior and include test coverage.
Use the skill for architecture guidance before generating large code changes.
anti_patterns: Do not apply zoneless mode to legacy apps without staged validation.
Do not treat placeholder API examples as production configuration.
Do not replace project conventions without checking existing Angular patterns.

faq.question: What Angular versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It focuses on Angular v20+ and newer modern patterns.

faq.question: Can it help migrate from NgModules?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains standalone components, direct imports, and phased modernization strategies.

faq.question: Does it run Angular commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but it does not execute tooling by itself.

faq.question: Does it cover Signals?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers writable signals, computed values, effects, signal inputs, and model patterns.

faq.question: Is it useful for SSR work?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes SSR, hydration, defer blocks, TransferState, and rendering guidance.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is structured for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
